A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original RAP-LLaVA and RAP-Phi3-V evaluations on personalized captioning, question answering and recognition, with additional benchmark results and ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds retrieval analyses, a RAP-LLaVA-OneVision sensitivity experiment and a qualitative robustness example.

M1.justification: RAP's database, detection, retrieval, generation and training procedures remain unchanged. The added 0.5B OneVision instantiation supports a sensitivity experiment; no new RAP component or procedural adaptation is described.

E1.justification: The training sources, personalized tasks, eight-pair captioning extension, MMMU and InfoSeek coverage are retained. The new analyses examine existing personalization and noisy-retrieval conditions. Appendix C newly documents collection of the existing multi-concept images.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds MyVLM-LLaVA to the standard captioning-metric comparison, which previously included LLaVA, LLaVA with retrieval and RAP-LLaVA. Other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds retrieval precision to the existing retrieval evaluation and introduces a captioning experiment varying K from 1 to 5 with RAP-LLaVA-OneVision (0.5B) and a 300-concept database. The main models' reported training and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 extends the retriever analysis with precision and adds a captioning sensitivity study on the number of retrieved concepts. New Table 11 illustrates responses with irrelevant retrieved concepts. Existing dataset ablations, concept-count analysis, timing study and perfect-retrieval test are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three captioning evaluations with different seeds and average results, including Table 8. v3 adds no revised run counts, uncertainty estimates, error bars or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain their numerical results, including RAP-LLaVA's 94.97 captioning F1. v3 adds retrieval-precision and captioning-sensitivity curves, the responses in Table 11, and MyVLM-LLaVA results in Table 8, including CIDEr 0.435 versus RAP-LLaVA's unchanged 0.388.

T1.justification: The retrieval-distance definition and autoregressive probability factorization are unchanged. Equation 1's presentation changes without changing its conditional-probability product; neither version adds formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about retrieval-based personalization, real-time concept editing, adaptation without further concept-specific training, and performance across personalized multimodal tasks.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes improved retrieval recall with larger K. v3 explicitly explains that retrieving more concepts introduces noise and can reduce captioning precision, establishing a recall–precision tradeoff in Appendix B.1. The original computational-overhead and retriever-dependence limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly explains that the existing multi-concept images come from sampled YouTube video frames, with detection and Gemini used to select frames containing concept pairs. This improves data-construction documentation; the principal implementation settings and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the LLaVA-OneVision reference supporting its new sensitivity experiment. The existing cited works and positioning relative to personalization methods and retrieval-augmented generation remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 polishes wording, adds RAP to the title, folds the main cost discussion into the introduction and moves the concept-count discussion into the ablation section. Appendix subsections are reordered, and acknowledgements, a supplementary title and an ethics section are added. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn. The existing retrieval-recall plot moves to the appendix beside a new precision plot; Figure 7 and Table 11 are added. Table 7 reorders rows, Table 8 gains a comparator row, and several displays are relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: The added MyVLM row in Table 8 provides a more balanced caption-quality comparison, while Figures 6–7 clarify retrieval tradeoffs that v2 only partly characterized. Appendix C also improves data-collection documentation. These address limited evidence and reproducibility gaps while leaving the core method and main results unchanged.
